title: A Five Sentence Term Paper Using Chi2 Analysis
text:
Introduction + Background
Many scientists for decades have pondered if it might be possible to create an app that would snap a photo of a book and then tell the app’s user information about that book including, for example, its genre which is the question we present and study in this paper.


Literature Review
Others have previously studied how machine learning algorithims may predict information about a book including a book’s genre (Vayadande et al. 2024).


Method + Data

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import seaborn as sns
from scipy.stats import chi2_contingency

domain = 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/'
path = "adamrossnelson/confident/refs/heads/main/data/"
file = "confident_fictional_books.csv"

books = pd.read_csv(domain + path + file)

Our null hypothesis is that book cover color does not predict the book’s genre while the alternate hypothesis is that book cover color does predict the book’s genre and we study this question with data from 359 books where we know the book’s genre and the book’s cover color such that we can conduct a chi2 test to see if these two varaibles are either independent or dependent (as it turns out our chi2 test will involve a 6 x 6 test).


Results

# Conduct the chi2 with chi2_contingency by passing the observed
x2, pval, degf, _ = chi2_contingency(
    pd.crosstab(
        books['book_genre'],
        books['book_color']))

Results: Chi2 Stat: 1.99210 - Pvalue: 1.00000 - Degrees of Freedon: 25.
With a Chi2 statistic result of 1.99210 and a p-value nearly equal to 1.00000 (degrees of freedom 25) we fail to reject our null hypothesis and conclude that given these data, and given this analytical approach, there is no evidence to believe that a book’s cover color may predict that book’s genre.


Discussion
It is a sad day for UW-Madison book club members, the DSHB students thought they could deliver a BIG WIN for book club members and book afficionados world-wide; the search for a reproducible method that will predict book genre carries on!


References


Vayadande, Kuldeep, Preeti Bailke, Ashutosh M Kulkarni, R Kumar, and Ajit B Patil. 2024. “Book Genre Prediction Using NLP: A Review.” How Machine Learning Is Innovating Today’s World: A Concise Technical Guide, 37–46.
